title: Humanized Mouse Models of Epstein Barr Virus Infection
author: von Boxberg, Gehrmann, et al.
materials: Human fetal liver tissue (procured by Cercle Allocation Services)
0.5 M EDTA, pH 8.0 for molecular biology (BioFroxx, 1353ML500)
Magnetic activated cell sorting (MACS) buffer (see recipe)
Direct CD34 progenitor cell isolation kit, human (Milteny, 130‐046‐703)
Furthermore, the number of seeded Raji cells per well for titration needs to be accurate to make the calculation afterwards as precise as possible.

steps.title: Transport fetal liver tissue cooled
steps.instruction: Minimize travel time and keep human fetal liver tissue properly cooled during transport; avoid delivery at room temperature to preserve CD34+ cell viability.

steps.title: Prepare digestion reagents and hood
steps.instruction: Set up the laminar flow hood, gather all reagents for the digestion mix, and have them ready before tissue arrival to save time.

steps.title: Digest liver tissue and mash
steps.instruction: Digest the fetal liver tissue, then mash it into a single‑cell suspension.

steps.title: Isolate mononuclear cells by Ficoll
steps.instruction: Separate mononuclear cells (MCs) from the suspension using density‑gradient centrifugation with Ficoll‑Paque.

steps.title: Enrich CD34+ cells by double MACS
steps.instruction: Label the MCs with CD34‑specific magnetic beads, run the cell suspension through a MACS column, collect the eluate, and repeat the labeling and MACS run a second time to maximize CD34+ purity.

substeps.instruction: Incubate cells with CD34 magnetic beads according to kit instructions.
Pass the labeled cells through the first MACS column and collect the CD34+ fraction.
Re‑label the collected fraction with fresh CD34 beads.
Pass through a second MACS column and collect the final CD34+ fraction.

steps.title: Assess CD34+ enrichment by flow cytometry
steps.instruction: Analyze the enriched cells by flow cytometry; expect ≥90% viability and 80‑90% CD34+/CD38‑ phenotype, with >10% human CD45+ cells indicating successful reconstitution later.

steps.title: Cryopreserve CD34+ cells
steps.instruction: Freeze the purified CD34+ cells in appropriate cryopreservation medium for later use in human immune system reconstitution of newborn mouse pups.

steps.title: Collect blood and harvest spleen from humanized mice
steps.instruction: Obtain immune cells by tail‑vein bleeding or cardiac puncture (performed immediately after euthanasia to avoid coagulation), then dissect the spleen and place it on ice immediately; process blood and spleen on the same day.

steps.title: Prepare spleen for single‑cell suspension
steps.instruction: Remove all fatty tissue from the spleen, mash it through a cell strainer, and replace the filter if it clogs.

substeps.instruction: Trim away any adherent fatty tissue.
Mince the spleen and pass through a sterile filter.
If the filter clogs, discard it and use a fresh one.

steps.title: Lyse red blood cells in blood sample
steps.instruction: Treat the collected blood with a red‑blood‑cell lysis buffer for exactly 5 minutes to remove erythrocytes while preserving lymphocytes.

steps.title: Surface stain for T‑cell subsets
steps.instruction: Incubate cells with the antibody panel for CD4⁺ Th1, Th2, Th9, Th17, and Th22 subsets; titrate each antibody if the signal is too high or low, using appropriate dilutions.

steps.title: Acquire and analyze flow cytometry data
steps.instruction: Run stained samples on a flow cytometer, analyze using FlowJo software, and calculate absolute cell numbers per milliliter or per spleen based on the fraction counted.

steps.title: Maintain p2089 producer cells
steps.instruction: Keep p2089 EBV producer cells in good condition by splitting them at an adequate frequency to prevent overgrowth and ensure fresh medium is always available.

steps.title: Scale producer cells for virus yield
steps.instruction: Expand p2089 cells for 2–3 weeks until the required scale is reached; then perform virus production over 6 days (transfection, harvest, concentration).

substeps.instruction: Expand cells in culture until sufficient numbers are obtained (typically 5 × 15‑cm dishes).

steps.title: Seed Raji cells for viral titration
steps.instruction: Plate Raji cells at an accurately counted number per well (exact numbers as per experimental design) to enable precise downstream titer calculations.

steps.title: Infect Raji cells and assess GFP
steps.instruction: Add a defined volume of EBV concentrate (e.g., 10 µL) to the Raji cells; after incubation, measure the percentage of GFP⁺ cells (expected 1‑20% of live gate). Subtract the 0.3 % background from uninfected controls to calculate the viral titer (~5 × 10⁶ RIU ml⁻¹).

substeps.instruction: Add EBV concentrate to Raji cultures.
Run flow cytometry to determine GFP⁺ fraction.

steps.title: Retitrate virus if infection low
steps.instruction: If GFP⁺ percentages are below 1 % or the signal is weak, repeat the titration using freshly prepared virus.

steps.title: Verify mouse reconstitution before injection
steps.instruction: Only use mice that show ≥10 % human CD45⁺ cells in blood for EBV infection experiments.

steps.title: Determine in‑vivo viral dose
steps.instruction: Prepare an inoculum containing 10⁵ RIU of EBV per mouse; this dose typically yields detectable EBV DNA in peripheral blood about 3 weeks post‑injection, depending on reconstitution level.

steps.title: Inject virus intraperitoneally
steps.instruction: Administer the EBV inoculum intraperitoneally to each mouse; the injection takes less than 1 minute per animal.

steps.title: Monitor EBV DNA in blood
steps.instruction: Collect blood at ~3 weeks post‑injection and quantify EBV DNA by TaqMan qPCR targeting the BamHI‑W repeat region.

steps.title: Generate qPCR standard curve
steps.instruction: Create a standard curve using the WHO International Standard; plot Cq values against log₁₀ of input IU to calculate IU ml⁻¹ in samples.

steps.title: Analyze spleen brightfield images
steps.instruction: Use Vectra and InForm software to train an algorithm for cell segmentation and phenotyping (CD20⁺EBNA2⁺ in green, CD20⁺ in red, negatives in gray), then apply it to multiple spleen sections.

substeps.instruction: Train segmentation model on representative images.
Train phenotyping model to distinguish positive and negative cells.
Run the trained pipeline on all spleen sections.

steps.title: Flow cytometry of CD45⁺ spleen cells
steps.instruction: Stain spleen‑derived CD45⁺ cells for CD19, CD3, CD4, CD8, and HLA‑DR; expect 40‑60 % CD45⁺ of total cells, 50‑65 % CD19⁺ of CD45⁺, 25‑35 % CD3⁺ of CD45⁺, ~70 % of T cells being CD4⁺, ~25 % CD8⁺, and HLA‑DR expression <10 %.
